question: A baby is born after a difficult shoulder dystocia delivery. Examination reveals the left arm held in adduction, medial rotation at the shoulder, with the elbow extended, forearm pronated, and wrist flexed — the 'waiter's tip' posture. The Moro reflex is asymmetrical (absent on the left). Which nerve roots are most likely injured?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Klumpke's palsy involves C8–T1 and affects intrinsic hand muscles, producing a claw hand deformity with intact shoulder and elbow function. Horner's syndrome may accompany it. The waiter's tip posture — shoulder adduction/internal rotation, elbow extension, forearm pronation — is the signature of Erb palsy (C5–C6), not Klumpke's.

Correct! Erb's palsy results from injury to C5–C6 roots (at the superior trunk of the brachial plexus) due to excessive lateral traction on the neck. The muscles paralysed are the abductors, external rotators, elbow flexors, and supinators — producing the classic 'waiter's tip' posture (adduction, internal rotation, elbow extension, pronation, wrist flexion). The Moro reflex is absent on the affected side.

Incorrect. Extended Erb palsy (C5–C7) adds paralysis of the elbow/wrist extensors and triceps — producing a 'wrist drop' in addition to the waiter's tip posture. The vignette describes classic Erb's palsy (C5–C6) without any wrist drop. C5–C6 alone fits the described presentation.

answers.text: C5, C6, C7, C8, T1 (total brachial plexus palsy)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Total brachial plexus palsy involves all roots and causes a completely flail, anaesthetic arm with absent reflexes and often an ipsilateral Horner's syndrome. The described baby has a specific posture with only shoulder/elbow involvement — consistent with the more common isolated C5–C6 Erb's palsy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Erb's palsy (C5–C6) produces the 'waiter's tip' posture: shoulder adduction and internal rotation, elbow extension (paralysed biceps/brachioradialis), forearm pronation, and wrist flexion. These movements result from the loss of deltoid, supraspinatus, biceps, brachioradialis, and supinator function. C5–C6 is the classic level.

Well done! Erb's palsy = C5–C6 = waiter's tip (adduction, internal rotation, elbow extension, pronation, wrist flexion). Klumpke's = C8–T1 = claw hand. Extended Erb's = C5–C7 = adds wrist drop. Total palsy = all roots = flail arm.
